card.name: Plural noun before a verb of existence
card.fires_on: The last word of a noun phrase in general web text, just before a verb or phrase saying where it is, how many exist, or what it is known for. Often a plural subject such as turkeys, species, rivers or questions.

modes.label: Plural subject before verb
modes.description: A plural noun naming animals, plants or things, right before a verb about presence or spread.
modes.example: Now, an estimated 70,000 wild tur<<keys>> are spread across the state.

modes.label: Superlative noun before a clause
modes.description: A noun after a superlative or 'first', before ever, to or now.
modes.example: probably the most successful scientific theory<< ever>> constructed

modes.label: Descriptive list intro
modes.description: A noun after an adjective like showy or fascinating, leading into examples.
modes.example: are just some of the showy<< species>> associated with the fall months.

card.writes: It seems to push vivid verbs of spreading, lighting up or dominating, mostly Chinese verbs.
card.plain: It fires on a noun that is about to be followed by a verb saying what it does or where it is found.
